<div class="markdown-heading" dir="auto">

# GUAC: Graph for Understanding Artifact Composition

<a href="#guac-graph-for-understanding-artifact-composition" id="user-content-guac-graph-for-understanding-artifact-composition" class="anchor" aria-label="Permalink: GUAC: Graph for Understanding Artifact Composition"><img src="data:image/svg+xml;base64," class="octicon octicon-link" /></a>

</div>

<a href="https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/3060102/204297133-9bf702c6-b4e2-46df-a029-42b5060b19a4.png" target="_blank" rel="noopener noreferrer nofollow"><img src="https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/3060102/204297133-9bf702c6-b4e2-46df-a029-42b5060b19a4.png" style="max-width: 100%;" /></a>

[<img src="https://github.com/guacsec/guac/workflows/release/badge.svg" style="max-width: 100%;" alt="build" />](https://github.com/guacsec/guac/actions?query=workflow%3Arelease) <a href="https://pkg.go.dev/github.com/guacsec/guac" rel="nofollow"><img src="https://camo.githubusercontent.com/4d1d123665072cd4200a390774a2631a187a00e86e861efbc3ba66affe52193d/68747470733a2f2f706b672e676f2e6465762f62616467652f6769746875622e636f6d2f677561637365632f67756163" style="max-width: 100%;" data-canonical-src="https://pkg.go.dev/badge/github.com/guacsec/guac" alt="PkgGoDev" /></a> <a href="https://goreportcard.com/report/github.com/guacsec/guac" rel="nofollow"><img src="https://camo.githubusercontent.com/ca2f712392255b4c33a5d53519e50c2e6438aa50f4baa1c1209f80f1c67bdf24/68747470733a2f2f676f7265706f7274636172642e636f6d2f62616467652f6769746875622e636f6d2f677561637365632f67756163" style="max-width: 100%;" data-canonical-src="https://goreportcard.com/badge/github.com/guacsec/guac" alt="Go Report Card" /></a> <a href="https://api.securityscorecards.dev/projects/github.com/guacsec/guac" rel="nofollow"><img src="https://camo.githubusercontent.com/8bc147cff0e23b2c2103e06e7875dd6a23271c91f5c6254ccbbc9473188e2e14/68747470733a2f2f6170692e736563757269747973636f726563617264732e6465762f70726f6a656374732f6769746875622e636f6d2f677561637365632f677561632f6261646765" style="max-width: 100%;" data-canonical-src="https://api.securityscorecards.dev/projects/github.com/guacsec/guac/badge" alt="OpenSSF Scorecard" /></a>

**Note:** GUAC is under active development - if you are interested in contributing, please look at [contributor guide](/guacsec/guac/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md). GUAC is an <a href="https://openssf.org" rel="nofollow">OpenSSF</a> incubating project under the [Supply Chain Integrity WG](https://github.com/ossf/wg-supply-chain-integrity).

<a href="https://guac.sh/" rel="nofollow">Graph for Understanding Artifact Composition (GUAC)</a> aggregates software security metadata into a high fidelity graph database—normalizing entity identities and mapping standard relationships between them. Querying this graph can drive higher-level organizational outcomes such as audit, policy, risk management, and even developer assistance.

Conceptually, GUAC occupies the “aggregation and synthesis” layer of the software supply chain transparency logical model:

<a href="https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/3060102/196563695-a1cdc8bd-9946-482f-873a-937bf75891dc.png" target="_blank" rel="noopener noreferrer nofollow"><img src="https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/3060102/196563695-a1cdc8bd-9946-482f-873a-937bf75891dc.png" style="max-width: 100%;" alt="image" /></a>

A few examples of questions answered by GUAC include:

<a href="https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/3060102/182689788-70acefc1-6d69-4972-abbf-3e60c0d4c014.png" target="_blank" rel="noopener noreferrer nofollow"><img src="https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/3060102/182689788-70acefc1-6d69-4972-abbf-3e60c0d4c014.png" style="max-width: 100%;" alt="image" /></a>

<div class="markdown-heading" dir="auto">

## Quickstart

<a href="#quickstart" id="user-content-quickstart" class="anchor" aria-label="Permalink: Quickstart"><img src="data:image/svg+xml;base64," class="octicon octicon-link" /></a>

</div>

Our <a href="https://docs.guac.sh/" rel="nofollow">documentation</a> is a good place to get started.

We have various <a href="https://docs.guac.sh/guac-use-cases/" rel="nofollow">demos use cases</a> that you can take a look.

Starting the GUAC services with our <a href="https://docs.guac.sh/setup/" rel="nofollow">docker compose quickstart</a>.

<div class="markdown-heading" dir="auto">

### Try in a Dev Container

<a href="#try-in-a-dev-container" id="user-content-try-in-a-dev-container" class="anchor" aria-label="Permalink: Try in a Dev Container"><img src="data:image/svg+xml;base64," class="octicon octicon-link" /></a>

</div>

The repo ships a [`.devcontainer`](/guacsec/guac/blob/main/.devcontainer/devcontainer.json) config that brings up the full GUAC stack (GraphQL, REST, collectsub, ingestor, NATS, and the deps_dev / osv / ClearlyDefined collectors) locally on Docker, backed by the published GUAC release image. Open the repo in VS Code with the <a href="https://marketplace.visualstudio.com/items?itemName=ms-vscode-remote.remote-containers" rel="nofollow">Dev Containers extension</a> and select "Reopen in Container" -- the GraphQL playground forwards to port 8080 and the REST API to 8081. Also works with JetBrains Gateway and <a href="https://devpod.sh" rel="nofollow">DevPod</a>.

## Supported input documents

<a href="#supported-input-documents" id="user-content-supported-input-documents" class="anchor" aria-label="Permalink: Supported input documents"><img src="data:image/svg+xml;base64," class="octicon octicon-link" /></a>

</div>

- [CycloneDX](https://github.com/CycloneDX/specification)
- [Dead Simple Signing Envelope](https://github.com/secure-systems-lab/dsse)
- <a href="https://deps.dev/" rel="nofollow">Deps.dev API</a>
- [In-toto ITE6](https://github.com/in-toto/attestation)
- [OpenSSF Scorecard](https://github.com/ossf/scorecard)
- <a href="https://osv.dev/" rel="nofollow">OSV</a>
- [SLSA](https://github.com/slsa-framework/slsa)
- <a href="https://spdx.dev/specifications/" rel="nofollow">SPDX</a>
- <a href="https://docs.oasis-open.org/csaf/csaf/v2.0/os/csaf-v2.0-os.html" rel="nofollow">CSAF/CSAF VEX</a>
- [OpenVEX](https://github.com/openvex)

Note that GUAC uses software identifiers standards to help link metadata together. However, these identifiers are not always available and heuristics need to be used to link them. Therefore, there may be unhandled edge cases and errors occurring when ingesting data. We appreciate it if you could create a [data quality issue](https://github.com/guacsec/guac/issues/new?assignees=&labels=bug%2C+data-sources%2C+data-quality&projects=&template=bug_report_ingestion.md&title=%5Bingestion%2Fdata-quality+issue%5D+FILL+THIS+IN) if you encounter any errors or bugs with ingestion.

<div class="markdown-heading" dir="auto">

## GraphQL backends

<a href="#graphql-backends" id="user-content-graphql-backends" class="anchor" aria-label="Permalink: GraphQL backends"><img src="data:image/svg+xml;base64," class="octicon octicon-link" /></a>

</div>

GUAC supports multiple [backends](/guacsec/guac/blob/main/pkg/assembler/backends) behind a software abstraction layer. The GraphQL API is always the same and clients should be unaffected by which backend is in use. The backends are categorized into:

1.  Supported/Unsupported: Supported backends are those which the GUAC project is committed to actively maintain. Unsupported backends are not actively maintained but will accept community contributions.

2.  Complete/Incomplete: Complete backends support all mandatory GraphQL APIs. Incomplete backends support a subset of those APIs and may not be feature complete.

3.  Optimized: The backend has gone through a level of optimization to help improve performance.

The two backend that are Supported, Complete, and Optimized are:

- [keyvalue (supported, complete, optimized)](https://github.com/guacsec/guac/tree/main/pkg/assembler/backends/keyvalue): a non-persistent in-memory backend that doesn't require any additional infrastructure. Also acts as a conformance backend for API implementations. We recommend starting with this if you're just starting with GUAC!

- [ent (supported, complete optimized)](https://github.com/guacsec/guac/tree/main/pkg/assembler/backends/ent) with <a href="https://www.postgresql.org/" rel="nofollow">PostgreSQL</a>: a persistent backend based on <a href="https://entgo.io/" rel="nofollow">Entity Framework for Go</a> that can run on various SQL backends. GUAC only supports ent with PostgreSQL. Other ent backends such as <a href="https://www.mysql.com/" rel="nofollow">MySQL</a> and <a href="https://www.sqlite.org/index.html" rel="nofollow">SQLite</a> are unsupported.

The other backends are:

- [arangoDB (unsupported, incomplete, optimized)](https://github.com/guacsec/guac/tree/main/pkg/assembler/backends/arangodb): a persistent backend based on <a href="https://arangodb.com/" rel="nofollow">ArangoDB</a>

- [neo4j/openCypher (unsupported, incomplete)](https://github.com/guacsec/guac/tree/main/pkg/assembler/backends/neo4j): a persistent backend based on <a href="https://neo4j.com/" rel="nofollow">neo4j</a> and <a href="https://opencypher.org/" rel="nofollow">openCypher</a>. This backend should work with any database that supported openCypher queries.

- [keyvalue: Redis (experimental, complete)](/guacsec/guac/blob/main/pkg/assembler/kv/redis): The default keyvalue backend, but using Redis as storage.

- [keyvalue: TiKV (experimental, complete)](/guacsec/guac/blob/main/pkg/assembler/kv/tikv): The default keyvalue backend, but using <a href="https://tikv.org/" rel="nofollow">TiKV</a> as storage.
